Class Order

java.lang.Object
app.order.Order
@Entity public class Order extends Object
A client's buy/sell instruction, tracked through its own status lifecycle (BR-04/05/06) — deliberately separate from execution, which lives in order.execution.Fill.

Lifecycle (KAN-93, BR-06): PENDING -> REJECTED when a trading rule fails, otherwise PENDING -> ACCEPTED, committed on its own as the firm's record of intent, then ACCEPTED -> FILLED once the fill is written and the user's available funds and the account's holdings have moved, or ACCEPTED -> REJECTED if the re-check under the row lock fails. Execution runs in a separate transaction, so an order whose execution fails unexpectedly stays ACCEPTED on record, with its reservation, for bounded-backoff retry. Conditional orders also remain ACCEPTED until eligible or cancelled; triggering is recorded separately from status. This entity is persisted as PENDING the moment a request is received, before the trading-rule pipeline runs, so a rejected order still leaves a record.
